name: Principled behaviour
principle: An AI agent acts by the principles in its own work, including holding back where structure costs more than it returns, and keeps every qualifier when it restates one.
state_description: Given a task, the agent does the sized, fitting thing: a one-line fix stays a one-line fix, a repeated copy becomes one shared place, a task is recognised as a task and not recorded as a problem, and the closing summary says how the principles were applied. A person who corrects it finds the correction recorded where the next session reads it.
hints_of_measurement: On cases that name the expected behaviour and the failure, the share of replies that act by the principle is high for every principle and higher than the same agent without the instructions, and the cases that need restraint or a kept qualifier pass as often as the cases that need structure.

name: Followable process
principle: Anyone applying ESOI can follow one stated order from purpose to selection by metric, sized to the work, and knows where to return when something changes.
state_description: A newcomer or an AI agent opens the steps, works through them without asking what comes next, skips a step only with a stated reason, and ends with linked records, a metric shown to tell good from bad, and a selection made by it. When something changes they go straight to the step it touches.
hints_of_measurement: Per trial: steps completed, skipped with a reason and skipped silently; times the person asked what to do next; whether the result passes the structure check with a checked metric. Silent skips and questions fall over trials.

name: Found structure
principle: Structure that already exists is found and reused instead of rediscovered.
state_description: Starting work in any project, you are told which projects ESOI is applied to here, how they relate and which file to read first, and the guidance itself names none of them.
hints_of_measurement: A question about where to look in a project is answered from the person's own index, including projects added after the guidance was written.

name: Calibrated judging
principle: A judge's verdicts agree with the human verdicts they stand in for, and where they disagree is known.
state_description: A reviewer opens the judge's verdicts beside their own on the same replies and finds few disagreements, each one named as a kind (too strict on restraint, too lenient on keywords). When the model behind the judge changes, the disagreement is measured again before the behaviour scores are trusted.
hints_of_measurement: Agreement with human verdicts on held-out replies, with false passes and false fails counted apart, and the share of labels that are a person's own.
